title: Generating Superposition of Transverse Ising Ground States by Quantum Interaction
authors: Koushik Das, Sayan Mondal, Ujjwal Sen
abstract: We investigate superpositions of quantum Ising ground states generated through a quantum interaction, in which the nearest-neighbor coupling strength is promoted to an operator acting on a central auxiliary spin. We prepare the central spin in a superposition, which allows the chain to evolve coherently under different effective interaction strengths. The states are prepared by adiabatic evolution of the joint system comprising the central spin and the many-body spin chain, followed by a measurement on the central spin and post-selection of a specific outcome. It is possible to prepare superpositions of transverse-field quantum Ising ground states belonging to the three magnetic phases, namely, the paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and anti-ferromagnetic phases. For a spin-1/2 central system, it is possible to prepare superpositions of ground states belonging to any two phases, while for the spin-1 case, the superpositions may contain three ground states, each belonging to one of the three phases. We analytically derive expressions for the magnetization, spin correlations, and entanglement of such states. The magnetization and spin correlations show distinct features in different superposition sectors. The nearest-neighbor entanglement is largest where the transverse field and Ising interaction compete, and its behavior differs from that of the magnetic observables. We also derive the quantum Fisher information relevant to estimating the Ising interaction strength. And it exhibits multiple peaks near the critical points of the constituent ground states, with the maximum value showing Heisenberg scaling, for the parameters and system sizes examined.
summary: This work details a method to create quantum superpositions of ground states from the transverse-field Ising model by coupling the chain to a central auxiliary spin. By controlling the coupling strength via adiabatic evolution and measurement, the authors demonstrate control over superpositions spanning paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and anti-ferromagnetic regimes. The study quantifies this control using magnetization, correlations, and shows that the quantum estimation sensitivity scales with Heisenberg scaling near critical points.
main_problem: The paper investigates the preparation and characterization of coherent superpositions of ground states belonging to different magnetic phases of the transverse-field Ising model.
main_result: The protocol successfully generates superpositions involving up to three distinct magnetic phases, and the quantum Fisher information exhibits Heisenberg scaling near critical points.
method: State preparation is achieved via adiabatic evolution of the coupled system followed by projective measurement and post-selection on the central auxiliary spin.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising chain coupled to a central auxiliary spin (spin-1/2 or spin-1). The Hamiltonian involves nearest-neighbor coupling strength promoted to an operator acting on the central spin.
key_observables: Magnetization, nearest-neighbor spin correlations, nearest-neighbor entanglement, and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
important_parameters: The relative strengths of the transverse field ($h$) and the Ising interaction ($J$), which define the paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and anti-ferromagnetic phases.
main_assumptions: The state preparation relies on adiabatic evolution and subsequent projective measurement/post-selection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the superposition sectors in the J-delta plane for spin-1/2 and spin-1 systems, and the dependence of observables like magnetization and QFI on the coupling parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and the state preparation protocol using adiabatic evolution. It then analytically derives expressions for magnetization and spin correlations for different central spin types. Finally, it analyzes the sensitivity of the state using the Quantum Fisher Information, demonstrating its scaling properties.
why_interesting: The ability to coherently engineer superpositions across distinct quantum phases using a controllable interaction mechanism is highly relevant for quantum simulation and understanding quantum phase transitions in many-body systems.
